chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: California contract trouble, returning to the Onyx and Maxine Sullivan
summary: After the Onyx, the group went to the Famous Door in California, hated it and left despite a six-month contract; back at the Onyx the band grew and took off once Claude Thornhill's find Maxine Sullivan sang.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And then we went to California. We went to California to work -- went to California to work, at the Famous Door out there, and we stayed there, I think about -- well, we had a little trouble there because nobody liked California. Everybody wanted to go back to New York, you know, so Stuff told me he was putting in the notice, and the guy said, "You can't put in no notice," the manager says. "You've got a six month contract where we can't fire you and you can't leave, you can't quit." So then we said, well, we'd never seen no contract where you couldn't put in a two weeks notice, so Stuff put in a two weeks notice anyway, we come on back, and Joe Helbart (PHONETIC), who owned the Onyx, he said, "Well, just lay around awhile and see what's happening." Because he had carried this band, but it hadn't gotten together right yet, see. Because when we first went in there they followed us
but they didn't do too good. They had Leo Watson and Pete Brown and Frankie Newton, and then got Charlie and Buster and Procope. , you know.
And little by little they weaved in, and they brought in to set it off, Claude Thornhill found this girl out there, and he called and said he had a girl out there and sing Scottish songs.
Maxine. And he brought her in to sing, and then the band took off then, you know.
